query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Surface modification techniques such as plasma nitriding will improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Stainless steel with standard surface finish.
generation.intervention: Plasma nitriding treatment applied to the stainless steel surface.
generation.conditions: Conducted in a controlled environment simulating extreme corrosive conditions (e.g., high chloride concentration, elevated temperatures).
generation.structural_mediator: Altered surface microstructure and composition resulting from plasma nitriding.
generation.mechanism: Plasma nitriding introduces nitrogen into the surface layer, forming a harder and more corrosion-resistant compound layer that enhances the protective properties of the stainless steel.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased corrosion resistance compared to untreated stainless steel, leading to a reduction in corrosion rates by approximately 20-50%.
generation.baseline: Corrosion rate of untreated stainless steel in similar extreme environments.
generation.boundary: Effects observed specifically in stainless steel subjected to plasma nitriding under defined corrosive conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The exact percentage improvement in corrosion resistance may vary based on specific environmental factors and the duration of exposure.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare corrosion rates of plasma nitrided stainless steel and untreated stainless steel samples in a controlled corrosive environment.
measurements: Composition analysis of the surface layer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of plasma nitrided samples is not significantly lower than that of untreated samples (less than 20% improvement), the hypothesis is falsified.
